races.name: Irish Stallion Farms EBF Maiden

runners_data.name: Always Magic
runners_data.note: Trainer Jack Davison has had a quiet 14-day strike rate (0/5) and this filly was eighth on debut over 7f at Goodwood — she is a natural closer whose position in the map understates how far back she will likely sit in a 16-runner 5f maiden, softening her prospects considerably.

runners_data.name: Dhikola
runners_data.note: Ran 7th and 10th in two 6f Good-ground outings for O'Donoghue, who is in decent 14-day form (2/3); a genuine hold-up horse by inclination who will not easily replicate her natural rear position in this big field, blunting her finishing threat.

runners_data.name: Eagle Eclipse
runners_data.note: Unraced debutant for J A Stack with Seamie Heffernan booked — going and style are completely unknown quantities, and the stable's 14-day record (0/6) offers no confidence, making this a pure watch-and-learn runner.

runners_data.name: Give Me Liberty
runners_data.note: Has form figures of 7-7-6 over Good ground for McCreery, who pairs her with Leigh Roche; headgear is noted and she wants to come from off the pace, but in a 16-runner 5f field she is unlikely to secure enough ground to make her natural late run, suppressing her chance markedly.

runners_data.name: Invincible Irish
runners_data.note: Finished 11th of 12 on debut over 5f Good for McLoughlin and carries the "fades in finish" flag — a hold-up type by style who showed no encouragement first time and faces the same positional squeeze as the other closers in this shape.

runners_data.name: Nando The Great
runners_data.note: Ran 19th of 20 on debut over 6f Good for Flynn and returned just five days later — both the bare form and the short turnaround are significant negatives, and a pronounced hold-up style offers no tactical advantage in this race shape.

runners_data.name: Walk On Harry
runners_data.note: Placed third over 5f Good and eighth over 6f Good for De Bromhead, ticking the course-trip box; a natural hold-up type but mapped to rear, and in this field his best chance rests on a compressed midfield scenario where he can find a gap from a handy position.

runners_data.name: Annie Tips
runners_data.note: Eighth on debut over 6f Good for Dowling (0/2 in 14 days); her inclination is to race from the rear and the redistribution to midfield reflects a field where genuine closers are stacked up — the "fades in finish" flag adds a further layer of caution.

runners_data.name: Arrowstock
runners_data.note: Best-credentialled of the prominent types with form figures of 6-5-4 across three Good-ground runs for McLoughlin; Ben Coen takes over in the saddle and this progressive sort, able to sit second or third, is ideally placed to exploit a front-runner's sustained gallop.

runners_data.name: Best Love
runners_data.note: Has a 4th over 5f Good, an unseated, and a 10th over 6f Good for the Harty yard; the 5f Good run is the key reference and a prominent racing style means she can sit on Southern Boulevard's shoulder and challenge late, though consistency has been an issue.

runners_data.name: Better Yet
runners_data.note: Shane Foley represents Mrs Harrington on a debutant — stable is in modest 14-day form (2/29) and with no public form or known style, this is one of three unknowns that could spring a surprise or be completely outpaced.

runners_data.name: My Irish Lady
runners_data.note: Runs for J P Murtagh (2/22 in 14 days) with Rory Mulligan claiming; form of 10th and 6th over 5f Good is moderate but she stays this trip and could benefit if the race develops into a dash from midfield.

runners_data.name: Ocean Surge
runners_data.note: Eighth on debut over 6f Good for McCreery, with a "fades in finish" warning and 61 days off the track — the step back to 5f may help but the form reads as one-paced and the layoff adds uncertainty.

runners_data.name: Southern Boulevard
runners_data.note: The race's lone front-runner for Lyons with Colin Keane — two runs over 5f Good (3rd and 5th) show she handles the trip and conditions, and uncontested supremacy at the front makes her the pivotal horse around which the entire race shape is built.

runners_data.name: Stormy Dawn
runners_data.note: Finished 12th over 7f Good for Fahy on debut, flagged for fading and returning after 36 days; 5f is a shorter trip than she has tried before and the hold-up style leaves her reliant on a chaotic race that is not forecast here.

runners_data.name: Syrah
runners_data.note: Debutant for Charles Weld with Patrick McGettigan (5lb claimer) — Weld is a sharp trainer with juveniles but no public form means style and ceiling are both unknown; the claim reduces dead weight but adds riding inexperience.

races.paceDynamic: Southern Boulevard is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with Colin Keane aboard for Gordon Lyons, will stride to the front from the gates and control a sustainable gallop on Good ground over this 5f at Cork. With no genuine rival disputing the lead, this shapes as a single-file, controlled race from the front — Southern Boulevard dictates the fractions, resists significant pressure, and the pace is unlikely to be truly searching. The field is packed with hold-up types — Always Magic, Dhikola, Give Me Liberty, Invincible Irish, Annie Tips and others — who are natural closers but are mapped to midfield here because the rear of the race is over-subscribed; Southern Boulevard and the two prominent types, Arrowstock and Best Love, are most likely to actually secure their natural positions. This race shape squarely favours horses racing prominently or from just off the lead, as a controlled front-running scenario on a flat 5f rarely allows true hold-up horses enough time to close from deep, making early position the critical advantage.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Front-Runner Controls Throughout
scenarios.trigger: If Southern Boulevard is allowed to set a comfortable, uncontested pace and none of the prominent types applies meaningful early pressure.
scenarios.body: Southern Boulevard dictates every yard under Keane, the gallop is steady enough to conserve energy, and the lack of a true pace duel means the leader hits the line with a tank in reserve; horses tracking the leader from second or third gain from the honest but not punishing tempo.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Racer Swoops Late
scenarios.trigger: If Southern Boulevard's pace is just honest enough to set up a challenge from the horses who sit second or third early and quicken off the bend.
scenarios.body: Arrowstock or Best Love track the leader within a length, bide their time until the two-furlong pole, and find a strong finish as Southern Boulevard's advantage narrows; the flat Cork sprint gives those who travel smoothly the chance to cut the leader down close home.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Tactical Shuffle Rewards Midfield
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely slow enough that the midfield pack closes the gap early and the race becomes a sprint for home from two furlongs out.
scenarios.body: The compressed field means several midfield-mapped runners — Walk On Harry, My Irish Lady or one of the lightly raced debutants — find clear running and pick off tired rivals in the final furlong; the genuinely held-up types remain at a disadvantage even in this shape because their redistribution means they are not truly positioned to close.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Late-Closing Surprise
scenarios.trigger: If the pace proves genuinely strong for a maiden and the leaders tie each other up, gifting a late run to a true hold-up horse.
scenarios.body: A redistributed closer such as Dhikola or Give Me Liberty, forced wide but with a strong late kick, sweeps past a tired front rank in the final 50 yards; this scenario is inherently unlikely given no pace duel is expected and the hold-up brigade are racing out of their natural position.

watchPoints.text: Southern Boulevard — monitor whether she breaks cleanly and gets to the lead uncontested; if Arrowstock or Best Love press her hard from the gates the whole shape collapses and the race opens up significantly.
Arrowstock — watch the draw and early positioning from Ben Coen; if he slots in second or third within two lengths of the leader he is ideally placed to challenge in either Scenario A or B.

Eagle Eclipse and Better Yet and Syrah — three debutants with unknown styles and capable trainers (Stack, Harrington, Weld) could inject an unknown pace or finishing element that scrambles the tactical picture entirely.

Walk On Harry — track where Ronan Whelan places him at the break; if the 16-runner field compresses early, a horse with a placed run over this exact trip and going could find a slipstream that his mapped position does not suggest.

Give Me Liberty — headgear noted and McCreery runners at Cork warrant attention; despite redistribution concerns, if she travels kindly in midfield and the pace is compressed, her 14-day trainer form (3/14) keeps her marginally relevant.

races.name: OCS Recruitment Handicap

runners_data.name: Kiss Don't Tell
runners_data.note: Prominent-racing 3yo from Daniel McLoughlin's yard; 254 days off the track is a significant fitness query, but the return to 5f from a 2/5f placing suggests connections have this target in mind, and Good ground suits on profile.
runners_data.comment: A runner-up effort last time out makes Kiss Don't Tell a genuine threat here, and she has run over today's trip and going before; the main concern is 254 days off the track, which leaves her fitness on trust.

runners_data.name: Amerilis
runners_data.note: Hold-up filly who has placed twice in five Good-ground starts and is well-suited by the 5f trip despite recent runs at 6f; the step back in trip with Donagh O'Connor up gives her a strong tactical angle if the pace collapses the field late.
runners_data.comment: Amerilis shaped with plenty of promise when runner-up last time out and again three starts back, and she holds strong claims as the top-rated runner in the field; winless in her last five starts, but her rating of 73 suggests she is on a mark she can exploit.

runners_data.name: Gonna Be Golden
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up type whose 3/5f on Soft shows she can hit the frame at this trip, though Good ground form is weak across eight attempts; Sam Coen's 5lb claim helps offset the OR66, but consistency is a concern.
runners_data.comment: Ranked second of twelve on our ratings, Gonna Be Golden brings experience of today's trip and going and last ran 27 days ago, but she remains winless in her last six starts and that inconsistency is the chief concern.

runners_data.name: The Right One
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner who won over 5f on Soft and has placed four times on Good; Ronan Whelan will set sail from the gates and the horse handles this going well, but must overcome Cashel Blue for supremacy and the two-way battle is the key risk.
runners_data.comment: Bounced back to win two starts back before a below-par latest effort, and The Right One has experience of today's distance and going in her favour; the main concern is reproducing that winning form after an unplaced return.

runners_data.name: Cashel Blue
runners_data.note: Course-and-distance winner on Good, making her a genuine pace rival to The Right One; W J Lee takes over from a trainer in form (1/6 at T14), and her three placings in five 5f Good starts underline that this surface and trip are squarely in her wheelhouse.
runners_data.comment: Cashel Blue showed she can find the frame, winning two starts back and third last time out, though she was out of the money in between; she has run over today's trip and going, but 137 lb from stall 12 gives her plenty to shoulder.

runners_data.name: Lilbittyprettyone
runners_data.note: Hold-up filly with limited form to recommend at this level; one placing from four starts on Good at 5f, and Rebecca Parsons's 10lb claim is the main practical argument for inclusion — form otherwise does not jump out.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last four starts, Lilbittyprettyone at least has experience of today's trip and going to call on, and 33 days between runs suggests she returns fresh; the 134 lb burden from stall seven, however, makes progress hard to fancy.

runners_data.name: Smart Sioux
runners_data.note: Hold-up type with a fade-in-finish flag; 125 days off the track, no wins or places on Good ground, and a pattern of declining finishes suggest this is one to watch with caution rather than follow.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts and 125 days absent, Smart Sioux faces a stiff task, though she has run over today's distance and going before and our rating of 63 gives her a shade of untapped potential to work with.

runners_data.name: Sceitimini
runners_data.note: In reality a true hold-up horse pushed into the midfield map position because the field is packed with closers; Seamie Heffernan's booking is the standout positive, but the fade-in-finish tag and 0-from-6 on Good ground make the form difficult to trust.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts and ranked ninth of twelve on our figures, Sceitimini is hard to fancy, though he has run over today's trip and going before and returns after a 42-day break with a fresh chance to reverse a run of disappointing efforts.

runners_data.name: Simmering Seas
runners_data.note: Another genuine hold-up type absorbed into midfield on the map, and the fade flag compounds the concern; 125 days off the track, no wins or places from six Good-ground starts, and a 24-length beaten run last time out at 6f underline the scale of the task.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts and returning after 125 days off, Simmering Seas faces a stiff ask, though she has run over today's distance and going before and our rating of 61 suggests some residual ability that her recent finishes have not reflected.

runners_data.name: Another Nice'day
runners_data.note: A true hold-up horse in terms of style, but the prominent headgear flag (p) and recent 7/5f course form suggest she presses forward more readily than her label implies — she is the redistributed runner most likely to grab a forward position in running; OR52 and 11d freshness are workable angles.
runners_data.comment: Beaten into seventh last time out and well below his one recent win two starts back, Another Nice'day ranks bottom of this field on our figures and looks hard to fancy at a mark of 52, though he has run over today's trip and going and a light weight of 124 lb from stall one offers marginal compensation.

runners_data.name: Lady Landhort
runners_data.note: Natural hold-up type mapped to midfield; bottom of the weights and placed on Good ground (5/5f) is her best form, but her wins have come on Standard and the STYLE_FIT discount applies — she is not guaranteed to settle in her natural position in this traffic.

runners_data.name: Love Bomb
runners_data.note: A hold-up operator with a fade-in-finish flag and visor headgear; trainer McCreery is 3/14 at T14 suggesting some stable activity, and she has won once on Good ground over 6f, but her natural style is compromised by redistribution and the fade pattern undermines confidence in a late run.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last six starts, with a string of mid-field and unplaced efforts making her hard to fancy, though she has run over today's distance and going before and returns on a reasonable 21-day break.

races.paceDynamic: The Right One and Cashel Blue are both confirmed front-runners and will lock horns immediately from the gates over this flat 5f at Cork, creating a genuinely contested early gallop on Good turf. With two horses determined to lead, neither is likely to yield cheaply, meaning the pace will be honest-to-strong from the outset and the field will be strung out early. Kiss Don't Tell is the most natural prominent racer capable of tracking the duel without burning too much petrol, while the bulk of the field — classified as hold-up types — will be chasing from midfield or further back. This race shape strongly favours a prominent-racing type who can sit just off the contested lead and pounce as the front two tire inside the final furlong; pure closers face a significant task over 5f when the race is run genuinely fast from the front. Several runners listed in midfield — Sceitimini, Simmering Seas, Another Nice'day, and Love Bomb — are true hold-up horses redistributed forward on the map because there are more closers in this field than positions at the rear can accommodate; of these, Another Nice'day (with a prominent headgear tag and recent course form) is most likely to force her way into a forward position, while the others will likely settle further back than their natural style.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Contested Lead, Prominent Wins
scenarios.trigger: If The Right One and Cashel Blue burn each other off and a prominent tracker swoops late inside the final furlong.
scenarios.body: The two front-runners fight it out up front on Good ground, setting a punishing gallop that leaves them vulnerable in the closing stages; a horse positioned just behind the battle — able to relax and conserve energy before striking — is ideally placed. Kiss Don't Tell, tracking from a prominent pitch, is the profile that benefits most here, with Amerilis also capable of finishing well from just off the pace if she can get closer than her usual hold-up role.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front Runner Survives Duel
scenarios.trigger: If one of the two front-runners — most likely The Right One — gets a decisive advantage and the other drops away, allowing the leader to dictate solo.
scenarios.body: If Cashel Blue fails to sustain her early challenge, The Right One can convert the contest into a solo front-running performance, setting a controlled-enough tempo to hold on; this scenario suits a horse with the tactical speed to lead and the class to repel challengers. Cashel Blue represents the mirror outcome if she is the one who powers clear and gets away from the field, having won over this exact course and distance before.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Late Closers Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If the front-running duel is so fierce that the entire field is drawn into a fast gallop, leaving the door open for closers to finish past tiring rivals.
scenarios.body: A truly scorching early pace can occasionally bring hold-up types into contention even over 5f, with the field bunching late as the front two capitulate; Amerilis, who has placed twice in similar conditions and handles Good ground well, is the most credible beneficiary. Gonna Be Golden, placed at this trip on soft, could also pick up late pieces if the race truly falls apart in front, though her recent form is inconsistent.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Race Collapses Into Chaos
scenarios.trigger: If the contested pace produces a bunched, messy finish with no single style dominating — gates, draw, and luck in running decide the outcome.
scenarios.body: With twelve runners over a flat 5f and a compressed field mid-race, any significant traffic problems or wide draw disadvantage could nullify form entirely, opening the door for a lightly-weighted runner to sneak through; Lady Landhort and Love Bomb, both at the bottom of the weights, carry least burden if the race degenerates into a lottery. This scenario is unlikely given the clear pace structure but must be acknowledged given field size.

watchPoints.text: The Right One vs Cashel Blue — watch for an immediate speed duel from the gates; if both commit hard from stall one through the first furlong, the race tempo spikes and the two front-runners become vulnerable to a prominent tracker in the final 100 yards.

Sceitimini, Simmering Seas, and Love Bomb are all genuine hold-up types mapped forward by necessity — if they cannot settle or get shuffled back further than expected in a 12-runner 5f dash, their chances are materially weakened beyond what their OR suggests.

Kiss Don't Tell returns from 254 days off — watch the market and early tracking: if she shows any sign of rustiness in the first two furlongs when she needs to be prominent, her chance evaporates in a pace-led race.

Another Nice'day has worn a prominent hood (p) and ran 7/5f on Good here recently — watch whether Orla Tynan (7lb claim) elects to push forward from the off rather than settle in hold-up position, as her true style is flexible enough to compete for a place in the front group.

Good ground is confirmed all-card at Cork today — no bias concern, but watch for any draw effect on a flat 5f as high-drawn horses in a 12-runner field may need to travel wider than ideal to secure position against two confirmed front-runners going hard from the jump.

races.name: Irish Stallion Farms EBF Firville Stakes (Listed)

runners_data.name: Alpine Wedding
runners_data.note: Ran third at this trip on good ground last time, handles the conditions and distance, and Pat Twomey's stable is in solid 14-day form (2/7); sits naturally prominent and will look to press the leaders from the outset, making this a straightforward tactical fit.
runners_data.comment: Alpine Wedding showed a placed effort last time out and has run over today's trip, but she carries 128 lb from stall ten and her speed rating of 59 gives pause — third last time out offers encouragement, yet she remains winless in recent starts.

runners_data.name: Alwaysanangel
runners_data.note: Joseph O'Brien's hold-up type won over 6f on good ground and clearly has ability, but steps up in trip and company here; Dylan Browne McMonagle will be hunting cover off the pace, and she needs a strong gallop to get competitive — her 2/2 form on good ground is the key positive.
runners_data.comment: Alwaysanangel arrives in fine nick after a win two starts back, has run over today's trip and going, and her rating of 86 heads the field; the one query is whether 35 days off has left her short of peak sharpness.

runners_data.name: Beibhinn
runners_data.note: Joseph O'Brien's filly has genuine form — winning at 6f on good — but the sheer number of prominent types in this field means she is unlikely to get her natural forward position; her style is compressed into a midfield slot against her instincts, which tempers her winning prospects even if her raw form figures are solid.
runners_data.comment: Twice placed in her last two starts and a winner three starts back, Beibhinn arrives fresh on 26 days' rest, with experience of today's trip and going and a handy draw in stall three lending her good claims here.

runners_data.name: Celtic Moon
runners_data.note: Won over 1m on good ground last out but finds herself back at 7f for the first time since a poor run on soft; a natural front-runner by inclination, she won't be able to express that in this field and Seamie Heffernan will need to ride her patiently in a role that does not suit — discount accordingly.
runners_data.comment: Seventh last time out blunts her claims, though she did score two starts back and her experience over today's trip and going suggests conditions hold no fears; the 128 lb burden from stall 2 is the other factor to weigh up.

runners_data.name: Damsel In Distress
runners_data.note: Ben Coen's mount won over 1m on good ground and is top-rated here alongside several others at OR 120; she naturally races prominently and should secure a spot just off the leading pair, with a 45-day break the only mild query — Daniel McLoughlin sends runners with a 0/7 14-day stat, so watch the market for fitness signals.
runners_data.comment: Ranked tenth of eleven on our figures, Damsel In Distress makes it hard to build a case, though she does bring a win last time out and experience of today's trip and going to the table.

runners_data.name: Film Set
runners_data.note: Aidan O'Brien's sole hold-up runner here has only one run — fifth over 6f on good — and steps up in trip and class simultaneously; Ronan Whelan will sit and wait, but the evidence base is thin and she needs this to be run at a searching pace to have any chance of involving herself.
runners_data.comment: Winless in recent starts and ranked last on our figures, Film Set faces a stiff ask here, though she has run over today's distance and going before and a trainer firing at 26% in the last 14 days offers some hope.

runners_data.name: Madam Secretary
runners_data.note: Ryan Moore takes over on this front-running filly who has been consistent without winning, placing in all three starts including twice at 7f on good ground; Moore's tactical intelligence gives her the best chance of controlling the race from the front without over-committing, and this represents her best chance of a first win.
runners_data.comment: Consistent without a win in her last three starts — placed third two starts back and again three starts back, and second last time out — Madam Secretary has distance and going experience in her favour, and a trainer firing at 26% adds encouragement, though her rating of 78 gives her something to find on the figures.

runners_data.name: Maeda Matsu
runners_data.note: Second on her only run over 6f on good ground, Robbie Colgan takes the ride for Sheila Lavery's small string (0/8 in 14 days); naturally prominent and must improve sharply in both class and trip to be competitive, but the good ground suits and she is unexposed.
runners_data.comment: Ranked ninth of eleven on our figures, Maeda Matsu faces a stiff task, though she returns on a quick turnaround of 11 days off a runner-up finish last time and has experience of today's going in her favour.

runners_data.name: Maire Rua
runners_data.note: Colin Keane's mount won her only start over 7f on good ground, which is exactly the conditions she faces here; top-rated alongside the other OR 120 runners, she will try to race prominently and her unbeaten record provides confidence, though this is a significant step into Listed company.
runners_data.comment: Maire Rua arrives on the back of a win last time out and has run over today's trip and going before, giving her a solid platform to follow up; the concern is whether 36 days off has left her short of peak sharpness.

runners_data.name: Nevermindtherain
runners_data.note: Aidan O'Brien's front-runner has been placed twice but winless in four starts, always racing on the pace; the fact she faces a direct rival for the lead in Madam Secretary means she may be forced to race hard early, which could compromise her in the final two furlongs — she's done her best work over 7-8f on good but the duel is the key risk.
runners_data.comment: Consistent place-getter who has finished third in each of her last two starts, though she remains yet to win in recent starts and a speed rating of 80 suggests she may just lack the necessary finishing kick; the trainer's 26% strike rate over the last 14 days offers encouragement.

runners_data.name: Shi Yang
runners_data.note: Won over 7f on good ground recently for Robson De Aguiar's yard, so the trip and conditions are confirmed positives; however, as a natural front-runner, the congestion of pace types ahead of her means she is unlikely to get the rail position that suits, and Donagh O'Connor will need to adapt her tactics markedly in what is a step up in class.
runners_data.comment: Shi Yang arrives on the back of a win last time out and has experience of today's distance and going, giving her a solid each-way profile at 128 lb from stall nine; the slight dip in form two starts back is the one note of caution.

races.paceDynamic: Nevermindtherain and Madam Secretary are the confirmed pace-setters, and with both intent on leading from the front, an honest if not fierce gallop is the likely outcome over Cork's flat 7f — neither is a true tearaway, but the duel between them should ensure the race is run at a genuine tempo from the off. Damsel In Distress, Alpine Wedding, Maeda Matsu, and Maire Rua will all press for prominent berths immediately behind the leaders, creating a compressed, competitive first half. This field holds more front-running and prominent types than the race shape can accommodate: Beibhinn, Celtic Moon, and Shi Yang are natural prominent racers who will be squeezed into a midfield role against their instincts, with Damsel In Distress and Maire Rua — both rated 120, class acts on form — best placed to actually secure the forward positions just off the pace. A genuinely contested gallop on good ground at a flat 7f favours horses who can race prominently in a genuine rhythm and then sustain their effort through the final two furlongs — the prominent, class-loaded profile is the one to be on.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Prominent Types Dominate
scenarios.trigger: If Nevermindtherain and Madam Secretary set an honest pace and the race is won by a horse tracking them in the first three
scenarios.body: The two leaders force a true gallop and horses settled just behind — Damsel In Distress, Maire Rua, Alpine Wedding — get the perfect tow into the straight to unleash their finishing effort; class at OR 120 separates them late.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front Runners Dictate
scenarios.trigger: If neither Nevermindtherain nor Madam Secretary is challenged aggressively and one controls the race at a measured pace, conserving enough to hold on
scenarios.body: A soft lead at this trip on good ground rewards the horse who controls energy expenditure from the front, and Madam Secretary in particular has shown front-running tactical grit in her three runs; Ryan Moore's pacing judgment gives her a clear edge in a scenario where the early fractions ease slightly.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horses Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If the early tempo is fast enough to compromise the prominent runners and Alwaysanangel or Film Set come from off the pace
scenarios.body: A truly hot gallop would stretch the field and leave late runners with ground to make up but with momentum through the final furlong; Alwaysanangel's course-and-distance profile and Dylan Browne McMonagle's ability to time a run make her the most credible beneficiary, though Film Set is one-paced and unproven over 7f.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Implosion, Midfield Surge
scenarios.trigger: If the early duel between the two leaders burns them both out and redistributed midfielders Beibhinn or Shi Yang manage to find a better position than expected
scenarios.body: With three natural prominent types shuffled back against their instincts, a collapse in the front rank could in theory allow them to swooop through, but their style-fit penalty and the strength of the OR 120 runners make this the least likely resolution.

watchPoints.text: Nevermindtherain vs Madam Secretary — watch how aggressively Wayne Lordan and Ryan Moore contest the early lead; if the first two furlongs are visibly quick, the prominent types behind will benefit and the front pair may pay the price late.

Damsel In Distress — 45 days off the track is notable in a fast 2yo Listed race and Daniel McLoughlin has 0 winners from 7 runners in 14 days; monitor the market closely for any sign she is not fully wound up.

Beibhinn, Celtic Moon, and Shi Yang — all three are natural forward-goers whose redistribution to midfield is a genuine tactical handicap; if any of them bounces off the gates and forces their way to the front early, it changes the complexion of the entire race.

Maire Rua — unbeaten but making a giant leap from maiden company into Listed grade first time; Colin Keane's ability to place a horse prominently will matter, but watch how she handles the step up in pressure if she's headed for the first time in her career.

Alwaysanangel — Dylan Browne McMonagle will be the furthest back of any fancied runner and needs the pace to be genuinely strong over the full 7f to have a chance; if the gallop is moderate, she will find herself with too much ground to make up.

races.name: NFP Irish EBF Platinum Stakes (Listed)

runners_data.name: Fort Vega
runners_data.note: Strong record on good ground (10/15 similar-going runs placed) over 7f, Rory Cleary aboard for Sheila Lavery's yard; a genuine hold-up type who will need a strong pace or traffic trouble ahead to get competitive from the back.|
runners_data.comment: Fort Vega has been a model of consistency in recent starts, placing second, third, and second in his last three outings, and with experience over today's trip and conditions he looks a strong threat at 133 lb from stall 12; the concern is that he remains yet to win in his last five starts.

runners_data.name: Keke
runners_data.note: Four wins on good ground and a proven sprint pedigree, though being dropped to 7f from 5-6f trips is a flag — W J Lee takes over and the horse will be held up off what may be a modest tempo.|
runners_data.comment: Keke won two starts back and has experience of today's trip and conditions, making him a clear danger carrying 133 lb from stall seven; the main risk is that he finished fourth last time out and will need to bounce back smartly.

runners_data.name: Carolina Jetstream
runners_data.note: Step down from 8-10f trips is notable and the yard fires at 10% over 14 days; goes prominently but form at this shorter trip and on identical going is thin (4 from 15 similar-going runs, no wins).|
runners_data.comment: Carolina Jetstream shaped with plenty of promise when a second three starts back, and she has experience of both today's trip and the prevailing ground; the concern is her more recent eighth and sixth suggest she will need to find her best form after 48 days off.

runners_data.name: Nancy J
runners_data.note: Murtagh's yard in good form (2/22 over 14 days); genuinely wants to come from off the pace but with multiple hold-up types in the field she is likely to end up further back than ideal, compromising her effectiveness.|
runners_data.comment: Placed third two starts back, Nancy J brings some recent consistency to the table, though she remains winless in her last five starts; she has run over today's trip and going before, and 128 lb from stall one gives her a straightforward enough starting point.

runners_data.name: Princess Child
runners_data.note: Dylan Browne McMonagle is an elite booking for Joseph O'Brien's mare; returns from 82 days off and hold-up style suits a strong pace that this lone front-runner may not generate.|
runners_data.comment: Princess Child arrives 82 days between runs and unplaced last time, yet a second three starts back underlines her class, and experience over today's trip and going suits; winless in her last five, she remains the one to beat on a rating of 112.

runners_data.name: Temperance
runners_data.note: Consistent at 6-7f on good going but the horse's instinct to be held up is likely frustrated here — the mass of hold-up types means she races further back than preferable, and recent form figures (558-60) offer limited encouragement.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts and ranked tenth of twelve on our figures, Temperance faces a stiff task here; she has run over today's trip and going before, and 23 days between runs leaves her reasonably fresh, but consistent mid-field finishes make it hard to fancy.

runners_data.name: Treasure Rose
runners_data.note: In career-best form with back-to-back wins and places, goes prominently which suits this shape perfectly; Shane Foley retains the ride and the horse's 11/12 strike rate on similar going is compelling.|
runners_data.comment: Ranked bottom of the field on our figures, Treasure Rose is hard to fancy despite back-to-back wins in her recent form — she was fifth last time out, and at 128 lb from stall 2, conditions look testing; experience over today's trip and going is at least a genuine tick in her favour.

runners_data.name: L L Koulsty
runners_data.note: Upwardly mobile 3-year-old with two recent wins at 7f on good ground; Rory Mulligan partners for a yard firing at 2/3 over 14 days — prominent style and light weight make this one of the more interesting profiles in the field.|
runners_data.comment: Ranked 11 of 12 on our figures and carrying 127 lb from stall 11, L L Koulsty is hard to fancy on ratings, though he arrives in decent nick — a winner two starts back and again last time out, 41 days ago, with experience over today's trip and going.

runners_data.name: Sindagan
runners_data.note: Ben Coen rides for the powerful Murtagh stable; won over this exact course, distance, and going trip (1/7f/GOO) most recently and goes prominently — the profile fits this race shape as well as any runner in the field.|
runners_data.comment: Sindagan arrives on the back of a win last time out and has shown consistent placing in recent starts, with a second two starts back and a third three starts back; he has experience over today's trip and going, though carrying 127 lb from stall nine and ranking eighth of twelve offers a measured outlook.

runners_data.name: Spinning Around
runners_data.note: Lone confirmed front-runner for Donnacha O'Brien, with winning form over 7f on good ground; gets a soft lead but faces the question of whether she can sustain the effort once the prominent pack closes at the 2f pole.|
runners_data.comment: Ranked ninth of twelve on our figures, Spinning Around faces a stiff ask, with back-to-back finishes of eighth and fifth in her most recent starts dimming memories of that win three starts back; she has run over today's trip and going, and 30 days between runs suggests she arrives fresh.

runners_data.name: Suzie Songs
runners_data.note: Colin Keane takes over for G M Lyons in excellent form; an outstanding 7/7 record on good going and three wins at this trip — goes prominently and the tactical profile suits this controlled-tempo scenario very well.|
runners_data.comment: Suzie Songs won last time out and has run over today's trip and going, giving her a platform to build on; however, the fourth and unplaced efforts in recent starts suggest some inconsistency, and 122 lb from stall 10 will test her resolution.

runners_data.name: Tahcawin
runners_data.note: Steps up from 6f and will be held up off the pace; Gary Carroll rides and the horse has placed at 6f on good ground but the hold-up style and step in trip in a race lacking genuine pace creates questions about whether he gets competitive.|
runners_data.comment: Tahcawin showed a flash of form with a third and second in her last five starts, though she has been winless in that recent run and a ninth last time out is hard to ignore; she has run over today's trip and going before and steps out from stall three carrying 122 lb.

races.paceDynamic: Spinning Around is the lone confirmed front-runner and should stride into an uncontested lead from the gates, setting a sustainable gallop over Cork's flat 7f on good ground. The prominent cluster — Carolina Jetstream, Treasure Rose, L L Koulsty, Sindagan, and Suzie Songs — will jostle for the handful of positions directly behind, creating genuine crowding and interference risk in the first two furlongs and again at the 2-3f pole as the field compresses before the final turn. The hold-up contingent (Fort Vega, Keke, Princess Child, Tahcawin) will be forced to find cover early and rely on a sustained gallop to bring them into the picture late, but with only one true pacesetter the tempo may not be strong enough to fully set up a back-end surge. This race shape — a solo lead, controlled pace, and a bunched prominent group — most favours well-positioned prominent types who can sit just off the tempo, track Spinning Around, and quicken entering the straight without being traffic-bound. The field holds more hold-up types than the map can accommodate at the rear; Nancy J and Temperance are genuine hold-up horses redistributed to midfield on the map, but in reality they are most likely to get shuffled further back than their natural position in a congested prominent group, limiting their effectiveness.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Prominent Types Dominate
scenarios.trigger: If Spinning Around sets a fair, uncontested lead and the prominent runners track smoothly without significant interference.
scenarios.body: Spinning Around controls fractions comfortably while Sindagan, Suzie Songs, and Treasure Rose settle just behind in the slipstream, producing a steadily-run 7f that rewards those with a clear run into the straight; the winner is likely to emerge from this prominent group that avoids traffic and lands travelling well at the 2f pole.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front Runner Holds On
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely modest and no prominent horse can mount a sustained challenge in the straight.
scenarios.body: Spinning Around, untroubled from the front and producing a frugal tempo, may simply find enough stamina in reserve to repel challenges on good ground at 7f; horses who hit the front too early and find themselves flat are the likely victims.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Late Closers Arrive
scenarios.trigger: If prominent congestion causes significant traffic issues 2-3f out, forcing closers to weave wide for a clear run.
scenarios.body: Fort Vega and Keke, both proven on good ground and comfortable at 7f, would be the chief beneficiaries if gaps open late; Princess Child also fits a scenario where a strong pace punishes prominent types who burned energy fighting for position.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos Produces Upset
scenarios.trigger: If early scrimmaging in the prominent group causes multiple interference incidents, scrambling the race shape entirely.
scenarios.body: A lottery develops with runners finishing out of order based on fortune rather than merit; L L Koulsty, lightly weighted as a 3-year-old with recent winning form, and Nancy J, kept fresh on 15 days, could each profit from the chaos if they find clear air at the right moment.

watchPoints.text: Prominent traffic 1-2f out — with five horses (Carolina Jetstream, Treasure Rose, L L Koulsty, Sindagan, Suzie Songs) all wanting to track Spinning Around, watch for early shoving and jostling that could unsettle or slow several of these runners heading into the straight.

Spinning Around's lead is uncontested but the pace may be too conservative — if Gavin Ryan settles into a very slow clip, prominent types tracking will travel effortlessly and the race could turn on a sharp sprint, suiting the quickest rather than the best-placed.

Fort Vega and Keke, both genuine hold-up types, are at serious risk of being caught in the slipstream of a bunched field if the fractions are modest — Rory Cleary and W J Lee must judge their runs early to avoid being boxed in at the crucial stage.
Sindagan's course-and-distance winning form on good going (1/7f/GOO) is the most directly relevant piece of form in the race and bears monitoring as a benchmark for how the surface is riding today.

Nancy J and Temperance, true hold-up runners displaced to midfield on the map, may drift further back still in a field this congested — watch whether either jockey elects to push forward early against type to avoid being buried.

races.name: Irish Stallion Farms EBF Give Thanks Stakes (Group 3)

runners_data.name: Ankara
runners_data.note: Hold-up performer for Joseph O'Brien who fades in the finish (headgear: t); sim-going record is thin (1 from 4, one place) and her sole win came over 12f — the extra two furlongs here is untested territory and a real query.
runners_data.comment: Ranked eighth of nine on our figures, Ankara is hard to fancy here, though she does arrive on the back of a third last time out and has experience of today's distance and going; the eighth and ninth finishes earlier in recent starts are the main concern.

runners_data.name: Bosphorus Rose
runners_data.note: Comes in fresh (45 days) for Paul Twomey and W J Lee with solid Good-ground credentials (3W5P in sim going); her last run was a win over 12f at Cork and she is the most natural prominent mover in the field with course and trip form to match.
runners_data.comment: Bosphorus Rose won last time out and has experience of today's trip and going, but a 45-day absence and a demanding 135 lb to carry temper expectations, and her form in the last five starts has been inconsistent.

runners_data.name: Nyra
runners_data.note: Dylan Browne McMonagle takes over for O'Brien on a mare who has placed in five of her last seven on similar going; her proximity record over 10-12f is excellent and she is well-weighted on OR 104, making her one of the most likely prominent horses to actually secure her ideal position.
runners_data.comment: Consistent and reliable, Nyra arrives here in fine nick — third last time out and a runner-up two starts back — with experience over today's trip and conditions, and her rating of 110 sets her apart in this field, though she remains winless in recent starts.

runners_data.name: Snapretend
runners_data.note: OR 99 stablemate for O'Brien who is a genuine front-to-prominent type by style, but with Nyra and Amelia Earhart also demanding that berth, she is liable to find herself further back than McCullagh would want; 83 days off is the longest absence in the field, adding another layer of uncertainty to a horse already racing out of role.

runners_data.name: Amelia Earhart
runners_data.note: Ryan Moore partners this Aidan O'Brien three-year-old who carries headgear (p) and has posted two wins on Good ground; form figures of 5-5 in her last two suggest she has lost some of her early-season sparkle, though Moore's strength into the straight should ensure she gets a clear run despite the prominent-sector congestion.
runners_data.comment: Amelia Earhart has experience of today's trip and conditions, and back-to-back wins four and five starts back show she can win at this level; the concern is three consecutive defeats since, including a fifth last time out.

runners_data.name: Believed
runners_data.note: Ben Coen partners this JP Murtagh three-year-old who wants to race prominently but is redistributed into midfield because the position is already oversubscribed; her three places from five on similar going (0W3P) suggest she finds winning hard but stays well, and if she does get into her rhythm she could fill a minor berth.
runners_data.comment: Believed is ranked seventh of nine on our figures, which makes her hard to fancy despite a lively recent profile that includes a win and two thirds in her last five starts; she has experience of today's trip and conditions, and 20 days between runs suggests she arrives fresh.

runners_data.name: Cameo
runners_data.note: Wayne Lordan on an Aidan O'Brien filly with a win on Good ground at 12f; five runs without a placing run in her last start (8th) is a concern, but she handles the trip and a prominent draw in a strongly-run race could flatter a one-paced type who gets a smooth lead.
runners_data.comment: Third two starts back reads as a solid recent placing, and Cameo arrives here fresh on 27 days' rest having already encountered today's trip and conditions; at 125 lb against a mark of 100, the weight she carries is the chief concern.

runners_data.name: Caught U Sleeping
runners_data.note: Colin Keane on the only confirmed front-runner in this nine-runner field; recent winning form over 10f and a place at 12f on Good ground underlines that he is capable of lasting, and with zero rivals able to match his early desire to lead, he controls the fractions entirely.
runners_data.comment: Caught U Sleeping arrives on the back of three consecutive placed efforts — third last time out, second two starts back, and a winner three starts back — though 41 days off the track is a query, and she faces stronger at a rating of 102 carrying 125 lb.

runners_data.name: Ice Dancer
runners_data.note: Ronan Whelan partners this O'Brien hold-up type who carries a visor (b) and has failed to finish better than seventh in her last four outings on Good ground; an OR of 85 makes her the lowest-rated runner in the field and her closing profile has simply not been powerful enough to land a blow at this level.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts, with a pair of ninths in her two most recent outings, Ice Dancer arrives ranked last on our figures and faces a stiff task here; she has run over today's trip and going before, and 37 days off at least gives her every chance to have freshened up.

races.paceDynamic: Caught U Sleeping is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with Colin Keane in the saddle, will stride out to set a controlled, sustainable gallop on Good ground over 1m4f at Cork — a distance where this horse has already won and placed. Four runners (Bosphorus Rose, Nyra, Amelia Earhart, Cameo) all want prominent positions, creating genuine congestion early and raising real traffic risk from the 3-furlong pole home as those horses jostle for the best ground. Snapretend and Believed are natural prominent types but have been redistributed to midfield on the map because the field simply cannot accommodate all of them in that band — both are likely to find themselves racing further back than ideal, which tempers their prospects. This race shape — a single uncontested leader setting a fair but not scorching pace — most clearly favours genuine prominent hold-and-deliver types who can travel close behind Caught U Sleeping without burning energy fighting for position, and who carry enough class to kick when the race ignites in the final quarter-mile.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Steady Pace, Prominent Delivers
scenarios.trigger: If Caught U Sleeping dictates a fair clip unchallenged and the prominent horses settle cleanly behind.
scenarios.body: Nyra or Bosphorus Rose can track the leader into the straight and produce a sustained, well-timed challenge, both boasting strong recent form on Good ground at this trip.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Leader Outstays Field
scenarios.trigger: If Caught U Sleeping quickens tempo at the 3f mark and the prominent pack is too congested to respond cleanly.
scenarios.body: The front-runner's improved recent profile over 10-12f on Good ground becomes a decisive asset as rivals burn energy negotiating traffic; Caught U Sleeping punishes hesitation late.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Storms Home
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace is honest enough to string the field out and the closers get a clean path in the straight.
scenarios.body: Ankara, dropping back from midfield trips with a win earlier this season, could pick up beaten horses if prominent runners have over-committed chasing the leader; Ice Dancer is simply outclassed at this level.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos In Midfield Muddles Result
scenarios.trigger: If the four prominent types clash for position early, causing a fractious pace that scrambles the anticipated order.
scenarios.body: Disrupted rhythm benefits redistributed hold-up types like Believed or Snapretend who find clear air late, though both racing out of their natural role means this is a low-probability escape hatch.

watchPoints.text: Four prominent horses (Nyra, Bosphorus Rose, Amelia Earhart, Cameo) all want the same early position — watch for hard racing in the first half-mile that could compromise all of them heading into the straight.

Snapretend and Believed, both natural prominent types shuffled into midfield by field congestion, may get cut off or trapped wide between the 4f and 2f markers — any interference here ends their slim winning chances immediately.

Caught U Sleeping's ability to control the tempo completely unchallenged is the keystone of the most likely race shape — if W J Lee sends Bosphorus Rose forward to test the lead early, the fractions accelerate and the race changes character entirely.

Ankara's tendency to fade in the finish (tagged in profile) combined with untested 14f stamina means she could be a false market confidence booster if punters read her single 12f win on Good as a reliable guide.

O'Brien has three runners here (Nyra, Amelia Earhart, Cameo, Snapretend, Ice Dancer) across the field — watch for any declared stable orders at the off that indicate which runner carries primary support, as Nyra with McMonagle is the likeliest protected ride.

races.name: Irish Stallion Farms EBF Fillies Maiden

runners_data.name: Chosen One
runners_data.note: Donnacha O'Brien-trained hold-up filly whose best recent run was a 2nd over 10f on Good; her natural rear-of-field style is squeezed into midfield by the sheer volume of closers in this field, which marginally tempers her finishing prospects.

runners_data.name: Elusive In Mayo
runners_data.note: A solitary run showed a fade in finish over soft ground at 12f; Thomas Gibney yard has been quiet at 0/7 in 14 days, and her true hold-up style is masked by redistribution into midfield — the step up to 10f on Good is a marginal positive but the form is thin.

runners_data.name: Emily Estherfaye
runners_data.note: Lightly raced, ran 11th on soft over 12f on debut for Andrew Slattery; headgear noted (hood), Good ground is a switch from soft, and the drop to 10½f suits better — raw ability is unproven but conditions are more favourable today.

runners_data.name: Fairylike
runners_data.note: First-time-out three-year-old from the powerhouse Aidan O'Brien yard, jockey Wayne Lordan, running style unknown — O'Brien's unknown-style debutants at this trip regularly carry significant market confidence and should be respected on pedigree alone.

runners_data.name: Garden Party
runners_data.note: Uncontested front-runner for Ryan Moore and Aidan O'Brien; two encouraging placed runs over 7f on Good and Heawy, steps up in trip to 10½f which is likely to suit her stamina profile — 291 days off is the key query but the stable regularly wins first time back.

runners_data.name: Quinchy Lady
runners_data.note: Two last-place finishes on Good ground at 8f, both showing a fade — John McConnell's filly has a natural hold-up style but zero placings, and the step up in trip to 10½f has not been flagged as a solution to her problems.

runners_data.name: Salamina
runners_data.note: Joseph O'Brien's hold-up filly ran 11th on Good at 10f just two days ago — the very short turnaround is a significant concern, and while connections clearly feel she can bounce back, her recent form gives little encouragement.

runners_data.name: Saxony Charms
runners_data.note: Consistent prominent runner for Colin Keane and A. Oliver, with placings at 3rd and 5th over 10f on Good — this is exactly her trip and going, she races from a position that suits the pace shape, and she represents the most straightforward fit for how this race will be run.

runners_data.name: Serendipia
runners_data.note: WJ Lee takes over for Willie McCreery's filly, who has shown modest form in four runs on Good at 8-10f; naturally a hold-up type occupying a midfield slot rather than her true deep position, which blunts her late-run potential in a race with only one genuine pace-setter.

runners_data.name: The Blonde Lady
runners_data.note: Debut runner for A.J. Martin, jockey Robbie Colgan — running style completely unknown, going unknown, but Martin occasionally produces sharp debutants and the lack of any form information cuts both ways in a wide-open maiden.

runners_data.name: Trumph
runners_data.note: Shane Foley partners this Mrs John Harrington hold-up filly who faded badly over soft at 12f and ran 8th over 7f on Good — the trip up to 10½f is a question, and her fade pattern is a recurring concern that makes her hard to support.

runners_data.name: Zadawa
runners_data.note: Dermot Weld's consistent hold-up filly under Chris Hayes has placed twice in two runs over 10f on Good — genuine form credentials for this surface and trip, and of all the closers in this race she has the most relevant and encouraging recent evidence.

races.paceDynamic: Garden Party is the sole confirmed front-runner and, ridden by Ryan Moore for the dominant Aidan O'Brien yard, will dictate from the front at a controlled, sustainable tempo over 1m2½f on Good ground — there is no obvious challenger to her lead and she is unlikely to be harassed into a suicidal gallop. Saxony Charms is the only genuine prominent type and will sit just off the pace, with the remainder of the field composed almost entirely of hold-up runners who will fan out behind. The field holds more hold-up types than the race map can accommodate at the rear — Chosen One, Elusive In Mayo, and Serendipia are all natural closers who will be shuffled into a midfield berth rather than their preferred deep position, meaning the true sit-and-sprint brigade is even more compressed than it appears. A steady-to-fair gallop set by one uncontested leader heavily favours those who can travel prominently and pounce in the straight without needing a strong pace to run into — the prominent-to-midfield profile, specifically Saxony Charms and any lightly raced O'Brien filly who travels well, is best placed to capitalise.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Garden Party Controls, Prominent Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If Garden Party sets a measured, uncontested lead and the race is won from the front two or three positions.
scenarios.body: Garden Party bowls along at a fair clip on Good ground and Ryan Moore controls the tempo, meaning those who travel up close avoid the mid-race shuffle; Saxony Charms, sitting just off the pace with good recent form at 10f on Good, is ideally positioned to challenge when the injection comes 2f out.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Types Quicken Clear
scenarios.trigger: If Garden Party's lead is modest and a filly from the chasing group quickens past her in the straight.
scenarios.body: A steady early pace compresses the field and gives the Aidan O'Brien unexposed runners like Fairylike the room to coast into contention and unleash a turn of foot; Saxony Charms and any well-travelled mid-division filly with class can also benefit from the bunched nature of the finish.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Types Finish Fast
scenarios.trigger: If Garden Party sets a genuinely strong early gallop that strings the field out and creates a truly run race.
scenarios.body: A strong pace would suit the genuine closers — Zadawa and Serendipia both have form on Good ground at 10f and show consistency, and would be ridden aggressively from their redistributed midfield positions to try to produce a late run; however, this scenario is discounted because there is no second front-runner to pressurise Garden Party into a fast pace.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Lightly Raced Filly Scores First Time
scenarios.trigger: If one of the unexposed, debut or near-debut fillies proves substantially better than her maiden status suggests.
scenarios.body: Fairylike or The Blonde Lady, both first-time-out O'Brien/Martin runners with unknown ceilings, could be precocious talents dropped into a maiden and simply outclass the field on raw ability; this scenario is the least predictable but backed by the presence of powerful yards fielding unexposed three-year-old fillies at a Cork maiden.

watchPoints.text: Garden Party (Ryan Moore/Aidan O'Brien) is completely uncontested at the front — if she is allowed to stride along at her own pace and quicken off a steady gallop, the race could be won from the front with a relatively low sectional, catching the entire hold-up pack flat-footed.

Salamina ran just two days ago and the extremely short turnaround for a Joseph O'Brien hold-up filly in a 12-runner field on Good ground is worth monitoring in the market — a market drift here would confirm connections are managing her lightly.

Fairylike and The Blonde Lady are both complete unknowns on debut; either O'Brien or Martin could be producing a well-prepared filly whose true ability is hidden by a maiden tag, and any significant market move for either runner late on should not be ignored.

With Chosen One, Elusive In Mayo, and Serendipia all redistributed from hold-up to midfield, the finish line closers are more congested than usual — if the pace slackens mid-race, this cluster of natural hold-up types racing out of their optimal position will struggle to find clear daylight in the straight.

Saxony Charms (Colin Keane) is the only runner combining a confirmed prominent style with directly relevant form at this exact trip and going combination — watch whether Keane uses that platform to position her just behind Garden Party from the outset, as that tactical move would be the clearest sign she is expected to play a leading role.

races.name: Fitzgerald Construction Building 'A' Rated Homes Handicap

runners_data.name: Launch Time
runners_data.note: Won at this course over 7f on Good and won over 8f on Good in recent form; Colin Keane takes over and will look to dictate from the front, which is natural territory — the STYLE_FIT flag reflects a prior run out of role, not today's likely positioning; the key risk is whether a career-high OR of 57 stretches this horse.
runners_data.comment: A winner last time out and third two starts back, Launch Time arrives in good recent nick after just eight days, though that ninth three starts back hints at inconsistency; he has run over today's trip and going, but 140 lb from stall 14 is no easy ask.

runners_data.name: Sheamus Seimhiu
runners_data.note: Returns after a 291-day absence for a trainer with a modest 14-day strike rate, and the long layoff combined with a fade pattern in finishes makes this very hard to assess; hold-up style suits a late-run scenario but the fitness question dominates here.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts and returning after 291 days off, Sheamus Seimhiu does at least have experience of today's trip and conditions and a rating of 60 suggests he retains ability, though his inconsistent recent form is the obvious concern.

runners_data.name: Half Cut
runners_data.note: Wearing a tongue-tie and stepping down significantly in trip from recent 10f-12f runs; the fade tag and poor form figures on Good ground (0W0P in three similar-going runs) suggest this is a significant ask at the shorter distance.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last three starts and ranked near the foot of our assessments, Half Cut faces a stiff ask here; he has run over today's going before, and 25 days between runs suggests he arrives fresh, but the handicapper's mark of 55 looks beyond him on recent evidence.

runners_data.name: James Henry
runners_data.note: Veteran of seven who has recorded back-to-back placed efforts at seven furlongs on Good, but his true hold-up style means he'll be shuffled into a more forward position than he'd choose in this massive field — the style mismatch tempers confidence despite decent course-going form.
runners_data.comment: Winless in recent starts, James Henry showed his quality with back-to-back thirds three and four starts back, and his experience over today's trip and conditions gives him a clear edge; the concern is his two unplaced efforts since, which he must reverse from stall 19 carrying 137 lb.

runners_data.name: Glamazon
runners_data.note: Shane Foley takes the ride for a well-regarded stable; has placed form over 8f on Good ground and the p headgear could sharpen focus — natural hold-up style but will sit closer than usual in a field this size, which may actually suit if the pace is moderate.
runners_data.comment: Glamazon has run over today's trip and going, and a win five starts back gives her something to build on, though her last three outings have been below par; from draw 11 off 136 lb, the top-rated runner here still has the profile to go well fresh at 30 days.

runners_data.name: Imnotleavinyou
runners_data.note: Won over 7f on Good and has shown consistent placed form at the trip; tongue-tie retained, and a race run at a steady tempo from the front suits a horse that can travel towards the head of a big midfield pack without losing position.
runners_data.comment: Imnotleavinyou won five starts back and has experience of today's distance and going, arriving here on a fresher 18-day turnaround with conditions to suit; the risk is that her recent form has been patchy, with three fifth-place finishes and an unplaced run since that victory.

runners_data.name: Dawn Flame
runners_data.note: Dual placed finisher on Good ground at seven furlongs with Dylan Browne McMonagle booked; tongue-tie and pads suggest a horse that needs assistance to concentrate, and the step up to a mile is the only mild query on a horse with a sound pace profile for this shape.
runners_data.comment: Dawn Flame has shown a degree of consistency with thirds last time and three starts back, but he's yet to win in his last six outings and his trainer is in a barren run of form; his experience over today's trip and going offers some grounding, though the yard's current record gives little encouragement.

runners_data.name: Mountain Memory
runners_data.note: The trainer-jockey combination of Andrew Slattery sends out this lightly-exposed three-year-old who fades in finish — only one similar-going run to go on, and that field was smaller; with a tongue-tie fitted and form figures of 5800, hard to back with confidence here.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last four starts, Mountain Memory at least returns with a 33-day break and has run over today's trip, giving connections something to work with, though a rating of 55 and recent unplaced efforts suggest he faces a stiff task from stall ten carrying 135 lb.

runners_data.name: Thompson Gunner
runners_data.note: Ran just two days ago, which is an immediate stamina and recovery concern for a staying-biased horse over a mile on the flat; his true home is held-up in longer races on Standard ground, and the quick turnaround combined with being pushed into midfield makes this a tough assignment.
runners_data.comment: Thompson Gunner returns just two days after finishing third last time out, so fitness is not in doubt, but the quick turnaround and a hefty 134 lb to carry are stiff asks; he has run over today's trip and going before, and that sole recent win four starts back adds hope for a competitive midfield runner rated 60.

runners_data.name: Morning Approach
runners_data.note: An eight-year-old returning after 20 days who fades in finishes and is 0W in nine similar-going runs; the true hold-up style is compressed into midfield by field size, and the weight of evidence suggests he will make up numbers rather than threaten.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last six starts, Morning Approach arrives on the back of an unplaced effort twenty days ago and faces a stiff task from stall 15 carrying 131 lb, though she has run over today's distance and going before and our rating of 55 offers modest encouragement.

runners_data.name: Borora Aura
runners_data.note: The only genuine prominent-style runner aside from Launch Time, trained by Mulvany who also has Imnotleavinyou in the race; placed twice from nine Good-ground starts and has the profile to sit second to Launch Time and potentially outstay the pace-setter late.
runners_data.comment: Borora Aura returns quickly on nine days' rest and has run over today's trip and going, but she is winless in her last six starts and her second three starts back reads as a lone bright spot amid a largely modest recent profile at a mark of 52.

runners_data.name: Peig Sayers
runners_data.note: A five-year-old with a fade pattern and a record showing double-figure finishes in five of her last five on Good; her natural desire to race at the back will be frustrated in a field this size — a tough spot for a horse that has never threatened to win.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts, Peig Sayers at least has experience over today's trip and going to call upon, and our rating of 55 suggests she holds more ability than her official mark of 44 implies, though consistent form has been hard to come by.

runners_data.name: Winston's Promise
runners_data.note: Three runs, three mid-field finishes on Good, and equipped with a hood; a genuinely inexperienced three-year-old whose hold-up instincts will be compromised by the traffic, and the fade flag alongside a slim form book makes this very speculative.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last three starts and ranked near the foot of our figures, Winston's Promise faces a stiff task here; consecutive eighths offer little encouragement, though he has run over today's trip and going before and returns on a sharp 17-day turnaround.

runners_data.name: Jazz Dreamers
runners_data.note: An eight-year-old veteran who wears a p headgear and has one placed effort from 15 similar-going appearances; despite genuine tactical craft in a hold-up role, being redistributed forward in a 19-runner field is far from ideal for a horse that needs a strong pace to close into.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts and ranked bottom of the field on our figures, Jazz Dreamers has little to recommend him despite the experience of having run over today's trip and going, and 20 days between runs leaves him with no excuses on freshness.

runners_data.name: Lorr's Girl
runners_data.note: Wearing a tongue-tie and back, with placed form on Good at this trip in her history; the redistribution forward from her natural rear-of-field position is a concern, but she has the physical profile to cope if the midfield breaks up — consistent without threatening.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts, with a string of unplaced efforts and an official rating of 40, Lorr's Girl is hard to fancy on these figures, though she has run over today's distance and going before and returns on a manageable 23-day break carrying 123 lb from stall 3.

runners_data.name: Mullacash Buzz
runners_data.note: Has placed three times from nine Good-ground starts at this trip and distance range; tongue-tie and pads are retained, and crucially the recent form figures of 3-3 suggest she retains ability — her true closer style is squeezed by the big field but she may find room if the race falls apart late.
runners_data.comment: Mullacash Buzz has placed in each of his last two starts and, having run over today's trip and going before, arrives with some relevant experience behind him; yet he remains yet to win in recent starts and his draw at stall 16 is a neutral factor with 123 lb to carry.

runners_data.name: Leannespour
runners_data.note: Three-year-old who fades in finishes and has run poorly in her two most recent outings; a step up from six-furlong handicap form to a mile in a 19-runner field asks significant questions, and there is no strong angle here from trainer, jockey or headgear.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last four starts and ranked 16 of 19 on our figures, Leannespour faces a stiff task here, though she has run over today's distance and going before and returns on a handy 20-day turnaround.

runners_data.name: Starflow
runners_data.note: Henry De Bromhead sends out this lightly-raced three-year-old after a 74-day break — the stable is in strong form (T14: 4/35), but the horse has no win and fades in finishes; a tongue-tie and back headgear are applied, and the layoff makes this feel like a fitness run rather than a winning mission.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last four starts and ranked 14th of 19 on our figures, Starflow has been consistently well held of late, and 74 days off the track adds to the concerns; the experience over today's trip is some comfort, but he has plenty to prove from stall 17 carrying 121 lb.

runners_data.name: Reponse Finale
runners_data.note: Won over 10f on Good and placed twice from 15 similar-going efforts; ran just two days ago like Thompson Gunner, which is unusual, but the form includes a recent win and placed efforts that suggest residual ability — the quick return is the primary concern, and no jockey is listed which adds uncertainty.
runners_data.comment: Reponse Finale won last time out but returns just two days later carrying 132 lb from stall nine, which tests her stamina for a quick back-up; she has run over today's trip and going before, though her recent form is patchy beyond that latest success.

races.paceDynamic: Launch Time is the sole confirmed front-runner in a 19-runner field and, with no genuine rival willing to press from the front, is set to dictate on a completely unchallenged lead over one mile on Good ground at Cork. Borora Aura is the only other prominent-style runner and may attempt to track, but Launch Time's rider Colin Keane can control tempo without any real pressure, likely producing a steady, energy-conserving gallop that suits those who can travel handy. The vast majority of this field are natural hold-up horses, but so many true come-from-behind types have been mapped into midfield simply because they cannot all get to the rear as they would prefer — runners such as James Henry, Thompson Gunner, Winston's Promise, Jazz Dreamers, Mullacash Buzz and others are genuine hold-up performers who will be shuffled into an uncharacteristically forward position by the sheer weight of numbers. With a single front-runner setting a sustainable pace and midfield becoming heavily congested with out-of-role hold-up horses, this race shape strongly favours horses that can travel prominently from the outset and sustain their effort through the straight — the tactical premium is on class and position, not a late sprint from the rear.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Launch Time Controls Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Launch Time is allowed to stride clear from the front without Borora Aura or any other runner seriously matching strides early.
scenarios.body: Keane settles Launch Time in front at a comfortable tempo, conserving energy while the congested midfield pack burns momentum jostling for space; the horse simply extends in the straight from a position of total comfort.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Trackers Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If Borora Aura or a handy-travelling hold-up horse positions just off the pace and swoops as Launch Time's lead is pegged back entering the straight.
scenarios.body: A moderate pace set by Launch Time tempts a few runners to close the gap sooner than expected, and any horse able to cruise into contention from second or third without expending energy fighting the pack will be best placed.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Midfield Finisher Threads Through
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses in the final two furlongs and a true hold-up horse that found clear running manages to pick off the tiring leaders.
scenarios.body: The sustainable gallop means the winner's margin is small, and a horse finding late daylight through an unusually congested midfield can still produce a finish, though the redistribution of so many hold-up types into the pack makes finding that gap genuinely difficult.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Tearaway Front-Runner Holds On
scenarios.trigger: If Launch Time is allowed to stride even further clear than anticipated and the chasing pack simply never has the quality or coordination to close the gap in time.
scenarios.body: With 19 runners and chaos in midfield, organised pursuit can fail entirely, and a horse that has already won at this course on Good ground simply gallops rivals into submission from the front.

watchPoints.text: Launch Time and Colin Keane — if they slip the field on a loose lead through the early furlongs, the 19-runner pack risks never organising a coherent challenge and the race could be over turning for home.

Borora Aura — the only other prominent-style runner; if Terry Casey pushes forward and challenges Launch Time for the lead rather than tracking, it could inject enough early pace to completely reshape the race and open the door for hold-up horses.

Thompson Gunner and Reponse Finale both ran just two days ago — monitor market moves for either, as a sharp gamble on either would suggest stable confidence despite the quick turnaround, but a drifter should be taken as confirmation of a prep run.

Midfield congestion is a significant physical risk in this 19-runner field — watch the first two furlongs closely as the redistributed hold-up horses jostling for position could cause interference that compromises several runners whose chance depends on travelling smoothly.

Glamazon (Shane Foley) and Dawn Flame (Dylan Browne McMonagle) carry two of the most accomplished jockeys in the field — if either travels conspicuously well through the congested midfield in the first half-mile, their ability to find cover and time a run could prove decisive.
